t: You're on Gerrard Street, in the heart of Chinatown in the West End. The street takes its name from Charles Gerard, the first Earl of Macclesfield, a Royalist soldier who fought in the Civil War, spent years in exile, and was made an earl by Charles the Second. The poet and playwright John Dryden lived here from sixteen eighty-seven. Dryden was England's first Poet Laureate, and he dominated the literary life of his age so completely that it became known as the Age of Dryden.
